screens.prompt: In B7, find the position of the month in B6 within A2:A5, counting the first row as 1.

hints.syntax: MATCH takes the value, the list to search, and the match type: =MATCH(B6,A2:A5,0).
hints.func-match: MATCH returns a position inside the list you give it, not the value in the next column; that is what INDEX does with the number.
hints.match-exact: The month list is not sorted, so the third argument has to be 0 for an exact match. Leaving it out searches an unsorted list and gives an answer you cannot trust.
hints.require-ref: Take the month from B6 instead of typing Mar, so asking about April is a one-cell edit.
hints.value: Counting from Jan as 1, Mar is the third month in the list.
hints.error: If the month is not in the searched range at all, MATCH returns #N/A: the position of nothing does not exist.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
without the third argument MATCH assumes an approximate search on a sorted list, which this column is not
a match type of 1 is approximate even though it happens to answer 3 today, and it would stop agreeing the moment a month was inserted
MATCH already counts the first row as 1, so adding one reports position four
the month typed into the formula, so the question can no longer be changed from the sheet
the searched range stops at Feb, so Mar is not in it and MATCH returns #N/A

docs.explain: MATCH answers a question about position: given a value, where does it sit in this list, counting from 1? The list runs Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr in A2:A5 and B6 asks about Mar, so MATCH reports 3. The third argument decides how hard MATCH looks. 0 demands an exact match. 1 accepts the largest value less than or equal to the target and needs the list sorted ascending. -1 does the mirror image on a descending list. This list is alphabetical rather than sorted by any rule MATCH can use, so 1 is a coin flip that lands on 3 today. Once MATCH has the number, INDEX turns it back into a value from another column, which is the pair the next lesson uses.

errors.text: The value is not in the searched range, so there is no position to report.
The match type was text, or the searched range was given as a single value instead of a row or column.

docs.atWork: Building the row number that INDEX needs for a two-way lookup, without hard-coding row 3 into the formula.
docs.outcome: Find where a value sits in a list, ready to feed INDEX.

seo.title: MATCH in Excel: find a value's position
seo.description: Mar is the third entry of Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, so MATCH answers 3. The third argument 0 demands an exact match, and 1 needs a list sorted ascending.
